events.did: stepped into EON, where two black-uniformed figures took his phone and scanned him before ushering him down a doorless hall
events.quote_anchor: two figures in all-black uniforms, who took his phone, and proceeded to scan him—presumably for weapons—before ushering him down a doorless hall.

events.did: swept the stylus across the bottom line of the NDA, signing his name and erasing his last chance of turning back
events.quote_anchor: Then he swept the stylus across the bottom line, signing his name, and erasing his last chance—theoretical as it was—of turning back.

events.did: tapped the tablet twice and turned the abstract pattern on the wall behind her desk into screens
events.quote_anchor: She reclaimed the tablet, tapped the surface twice, and the pattern on the wall behind her melted into screens.

events.did: explained that EON was created to hunt down, capture and contain the ExtraOrdinaries
events.quote_anchor: EON was created to hunt down, capture, and contain them. In short, to neutralize the threat they pose to society at large.

events.did: recalled the scalpel in his hand cutting across the other doctor's throat
events.quote_anchor: Gabriel saw the scalpel in his hand. How easily it cut across the other doctor’s throat.

events.did: left the office by walking through the wall as if it were a curtain
events.quote_anchor: Then she turned on her heel and left the office. Not through the door, but through the wall, passing straight through as if it were a curtain.

events.did: returned a moment later holding a small blue wildflower picked in the field behind the building
events.quote_anchor: A moment later, Rios returned. The only difference was that she now held a small blue wildflower in one hand.

events.did: described the EO she caught second, who drowned six people by accident, as not meaning to be dangerous but being dangerous anyway
events.quote_anchor: The next one drowned six people by accident. The first meant to be dangerous, the second didn’t, but both of them were.

relations.did: hired Gabriel to find out what makes the EOs tick and why they alone were able to cheat death
relations.quote_anchor: To do that, I need to know what makes them tick. Why they alone were able to cheat death.

relations.did: was Helena's predecessor and thought EO power could be harnessed and put to use in the service of EON
relations.quote_anchor: My predecessor, Stell, shared that sentiment. He thought their power could be harnessed, and put to use, in the service of EON.

relations.did: was murdered by an EO, and his experiment was discontinued
relations.quote_anchor: “He was murdered,” she said flatly. “By an EO. Admittedly, not one of his. But suffice to say, his experiment was discontinued.

relations.did: was found by EON and given a choice, by Stell, to serve instead of being locked up
relations.quote_anchor: “EON found me,” she said evenly. “And they gave me a choice.

numbers.did: waited three days before calling the number on the card
numbers.quote_anchor: Gabriel had waited three days to call the number on the card.

numbers.did: counted ten, twenty, thirty steps before his escorts turned the corner
numbers.quote_anchor: He counted the steps as they walked—ten, twenty, thirty—before his escorts turned a corner, and he saw Director Roy

numbers.who: the wall of screens behind Helena's desk
numbers.did: held two dozen screens showing live feeds of doors, corridors and rooms
numbers.quote_anchor: melted into screens. Two dozen of them, live feeds of doors, and corridors, and rooms.

numbers.who: the EO on one of the screens
numbers.did: floated two feet off the floor
numbers.quote_anchor: But on one screen, a man floated two feet off the floor.
The next one drowned six people by accident.

numbers.did: served in the marines for seven years before serving EON
numbers.quote_anchor: I was in the marines, for seven years. I chose to serve my country then. I choose to serve it now.
